title: VPC/on-prem Handoff Runbook — Staging to Prod Cutover & Rolling Instance Rotation
content:
Purpose:
This runbook documents a pragmatic, low-risk approach for handing off a private control plane deployment from staging to production environments in a customer VPC / on-prem setup. It focuses on the cutover steps, rolling instance rotations (drain/replace), Terraform module considerations, and upgrade/rollback plans. It is intentionally prescriptive to minimize ambiguity during ops windows and on-call transitions.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: single-region private control plane (control-plane services + metadata DB + API gateway) installed in customer VPC or on-prem cluster.
- Kubernetes used for control plane components (k8s version pinned per customer), Terraform for infra provisioning, S3-compatible backend for tfstate with locking.
- Existing staging environment reflects production configuration; staging has had a successful smoke pass.
- Network, firewall, LDAP/KMS credentials provisioned by customer prior to cutover.
- This document is NOT a replacement for customer-specific runbooks (network diagrams, CMDB entries).

Pre-cutover checklist (run at least 72h before):
1) Stakeholder confirmations: product engineering, on-call SRE, customer infra lead, security contact, and release manager all booked.
2) Backup tfstate snapshot: create snapshot of remote state (s3://customer-terraform-state/backups/yyyy-mm-dd). Verify integrity.
3) DB snapshot: take logical backup of metadata DB and record snapshot id/retention.
4) Certs/keys: verify TLS cert chain and KMS/HSM key access; rotate test key in staging and confirm decryption for service tokens.
5) Capacity plan: node counts, expected RPS, burst allowance. Ensure dedicated nodes for control plane (no user workloads).
6) Monitoring/alerts: ensure dashboards imported to prod: API latency, error-rate, pod restarts, CPU/GPU, disk pressure, etc. Set temporary lowered thresholds for the cutover window to detect regressions early.
7) Terraform module and provider versions: lock module versions (see Terraform notes section).
8) Deployment window & maintenance page: schedule DNS TTL reductions and a short maintenance window if needed; communicate to customer and internal teams.

Cutover approach (high level):
- Deploy infra changes with Terraform in prod workspace (non-destructive where possible).
- Perform rolling instance rotation for control plane components that require restart/upgrade.
- Incrementally shift traffic from staging endpoints to prod endpoints using canary DNS and health checks.
- Validate and then finalize DNS/TLS cutover.

Step-by-step run (recommended ordering):
A. PREP: reduce DNS TTLs (if controlling) to 60s; set maintenance banner.
B. LOCK STATE: ensure no concurrent Terraform users. Acquire remote backend lock.
C. TF PLAN: terraform workspace select prod; terraform init -upgrade; terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=tfplan-prod.out.
   - Review plan with team; pay attention to resource replacements ("-/+" semantics).
D. TF APPLY: terraform apply tfplan-prod.out. Use --parallelism=10 for large infra only if provider tested.
   - If plan includes resource replacement of stateful components (DB, storage), abort and review; prefer creating parallel resources and cutover at application layer.
E. POST-APPLY VALIDATION: verify expected node counts, security groups, route tables, and load balancer targets.
F. CONTROL PLANE ROLL: perform rolling restart/rotation per component (API gateway -> control-plane-api -> controllers -> caches) with the drain sequence below.
G. HEALTH CANARY: shift 5-10% traffic for 15 minutes, verify metrics, expand to 50% for 30 minutes, then 100% if green.
H. FINALIZE: raise DNS TTL back, remove maintenance banner, run post-cutover smoke tests and capture artifacts.

Rolling instance rotation (drain & replace) — per-node procedure:
- Purpose: safely rotate nodes (k8s or VMs) that host control-plane pods without dropping in-flight requests or losing required quorum (etcd/DB).
- Preconditions: cluster has >2x minimum nodes for control-plane; etcd snapshots healthy and replicated; quorum will remain after one node removal.

Steps: (for each node, one-at-a-time unless capacity planning allows two)
1) Mark node unschedulable: kubectl cordon <node>.
2) Drain pods (graceful): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m.
   - Watch for long-running requests in API gateway; wait for in-flight warmups to finish.
   - If pods fail to terminate after threshold, escalate to SRE lead.
3) Remove from LB / route tables: take the instance out of target group (if applicable) to prevent new connections.
4) Replace node: run Terraform to provision new node or reprovision with orchestration: terraform apply -target=module.node_pool["name"].instance["i"].  (Prefer controlled tf target only for node replacement.)
5) Wait for node to join cluster and pass readiness probes; kubectl uncordon when ready.
6) Rebalance caches: invalidate local caches for components that used node-local caches (prefix/KV caches).
7) Verify: confirm pod distribution, CPU/GPU utilization, pod restart counts, and latency percentiles within expected bounds for 20m.

Emergency stop/rollback during rotation:
- If multiple health checks breach or etcd loses quorum: immediately stop further node drains, re-add previously removed nodes to LB, and if needed restore etcd using latest snapshot. Follow DB restore plan documented in linked artifacts.

Terraform module notes (practical war stories & constraints):
- Use pinned module versions: registry module private-cp-network v2.1.0, private-cp-cluster v3.0.2. Add a modules.lock file in repo.
- Remote state: s3-compatible with object lock disabled; use DynamoDB-style lock table. Create on-demand backups before any apply.
- Workspaces: use explicit workspaces (prod/staging) and never share the same backend key across workspaces.
- plan -> out -> apply flow is mandatory for production. Keep plan outputs (.out) archived for audit.
- Avoid in-place replacement of volumes that hold persistent etcd data. Prefer creating new cluster members and performing a controlled join/drain of old members.
- When performing provider upgrades: run terraform init -upgrade in a disposable CI ephemeral runner first; validate plan there and then replicate locally.

Upgrade strategy (control plane components):
- Minor patches: rolling restarts with health checks (no DB migrations expected).
- Minor version bumps with DB migration: create migration-runner job in staging, run against snapshot to time migration duration, then schedule timeline.
- Major version changes: blue/green when possible. Provision new control plane with new version, sync state elements (where compatible), promote traffic. If stateful incompatibilities exist, coordinate DB migration window (prepare rollback data export).

Smoke & validation checklist post-cutover (run within 15m, 1h, 4h):
- 15m: API 200 ok for health endpoints; 95p latency <= baseline +10%; errors <= baseline +0.5% absolute.
- 1h: trace sampling looks healthy, no new high-severity errors, metrics stabilized.
- 4h: full load test at 50% expected peak for 15m; observe RLs, token throughput for generation endpoints, and embedding latency.
- Logs: search for 5xx spikes, KMS decryption errors, TLS handshake failures.

Observability queries (Prometheus / Kibana examples):
- Prometheus:  sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="cp-api",status!~"2.."}[5m])) by (status)
- Latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="cp-api"}[5m])) by (le))
- Kibana: source: "cp-api" AND message: "error" AND timestamp:[now-1h TO now] sorted by timestamp desc

Rollback plan (if critical):
1) Halt traffic shift and snap DNS/Load balancer back to staging endpoints or prior endpoint IPs.
2) If Terraform applied changes that replaced resources: restore tfstate snapshot from backups and run terraform apply with restored state in dry-run mode to reconcile.
3) If DB migration caused incompatibility: restore DB from pre-cutover snapshot and replay any necessary idempotent events.
4) Communicate rollback completion with schedule for reattempt or postmortem.

Postcutover housekeeping:
- Rotate keys/certs if short-lived.
- Revert temporary low alert thresholds after 24h if metrics stable.
- Tag terraform state backups and archive plan artifacts to the release ticket.
- Run a brief RCA capture: what went well, unexpected issues, time to detect/mitigate, suggested improvements.

Runbook appendices (quick commands and handy reminders):
- Terraform workflow: terraform workspace select prod && terraform init -upgrade && terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out tfplan.out && terraform apply tfplan.out
- Acquire lock check: aws dynamodb list-tables --region us-east-1 (verify lock table entries)
- etcd backup: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=<etcd-endpoints> --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/client.crt --key=/etc/etcd/client.key
- KMS test decrypt: aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://token.enc --output text --query Plaintext | base64 --decode

Open questions / follow-ups before next ops window:
- Formalize preflight terraform CI job that spits an automated diff between staging and prod workspaces.
- Add a small ephemeral chaos test in staging to verify drain semantics for the most critical pods.
- Confirm runbook alignment with customer network runbooks (NAT, egress, proxy).

Notes from last rehearsal (2025-09-12):
- Observed 2-minute delay for LB membership propagation for customer B; add a 3-minute wait after removing/adding LB targets.
- DNS TTL rollback was not performed; reduced TTL warnings added to checklist.
- One-off kubelet crash on older OS image; escalate to release-engineering to include image compatibility matrix.

Owner & escalation contacts:
- Runbook owner: Aisha Ramirez (on-call/responsible)
- Primary SRE: Kenji Watanabe (pager)
- Infra eng lead: Marta Liu (Slack @marta)
notes: This is a working runbook intended to be adapted per-customer. Keep changes minimal and document modifications in the linked artifacts (PRs and Jira).
